one_liner: Kyle Tucker posted a .371 estimated wOBA on contact despite an unremarkable 83.7 mph average exit velocity.
three_things: The gap is the story: .371 contact quality on 83.7 mph average exit velocity.
The top end explains part of it -- 102.5 mph at the 90th percentile.
733 batted balls out of 2,216 pitches seen.
context_note: Descriptive only, from a single 2025 Statcast pull (pitches_faced_2025>=300 floor, 485 of 671 batters). The contact numbers -- exit velocity and estimated wOBA on contact -- cover the batted balls only, not every pitch seen, and estimated wOBA on contact is a batted-ball model: it says nothing about walks, strikeouts, or actual results. This pull carries no swing/miss or launch-angle column, so there is no whiff rate and no barrel profile here. Not park-, role-, or opponent-adjusted, and not a prediction. A high estimated wOBA on contact alongside an ordinary average exit velocity usually points at launch angle or spray direction -- neither of which is in this pull, so the mechanism is not identified here.
